God explicitly motivates Moses's leadership role by stating: 'Behold, the cry of the children of Israel has come to me, and I have also seen the oppression with which Egypt is oppressing them' (וְעַתָּ֕ה הִנֵּ֛ה צַעֲקַ֥ת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֣אָה אֵלָ֑י וְגַם־ רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ הַלַּ֔חַץ). God then sends Moses to deliver the people from their suffering. The narrative structure establishes that the foundation of leadership—both divine and human—is responsive care for the people's welfare. Additionally, Moses is initially described as a shepherd (רֹעֶ֛ה), a metaphor that reinforces the caring stewardship expected of a leader. The text presents leadership as fundamentally rooted in addressing and alleviating the suffering of the common people.
